inlines.text: When two circles intersect, the line joining their centres is the perpendicular bisector of their common chord.

spec.description: Two unequal intersecting circles, with centres O and P on a horizontal line. Their common chord AB meets OP at M. Dashed red auxiliary radii distinguish the proof triangles. Ordinary source-blue geometry is reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: A and B lie on both circles; OA=OB and PA=PB are radii. O, M and P are collinear, and A, M and B are collinear. No equality or right-angle marks are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and auxiliary segments are visible; no proof conclusions are marked.

answer.worked:
In triangles $AOP$ and $BOP$:
$$\begin{align*}AO&=BO &&\text{(radii of the circle with centre }O\text{)}\\AP&=BP &&\text{(radii of the circle with centre }P\text{)}\\OP&=OP &&\text{(common side)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle AOP\equiv\triangle BOP$ (SSS).

answer.short: $\angle AOP=\angle BOP$ (matching angles of congruent triangles), so $OP$ bisects $\angle AOB$.
answer.worked: From part a, $\angle AOP=\angle BOP$ because matching angles of congruent triangles are equal. Thus $OP$ divides $\angle AOB$ into two equal angles, so $OP$ bisects $\angle AOB$.

answer.short: $\triangle AOM\equiv\triangle BOM$ (SAS): $OA=OB$, $\angle AOM=\angle BOM$ and $OM$ is common.
answer.worked:
In triangles $AOM$ and $BOM$:
$$\begin{align*}OA&=OB &&\text{(radii)}\\\angle AOM&=\angle BOM &&\text{(part b, since }O,M,P\text{ are collinear)}\\OM&=OM &&\text{(common side)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle AOM\equiv\triangle BOM$ (SAS).

answer.short:
$AM=BM$ and $AB\perp OP$.

Matching sides give $AM=BM$; the equal adjacent angles at $M$ are supplementary, so each is $90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
From part c, $AM=BM$ and $\angle AMO=\angle BMO$ (matching sides and angles of congruent triangles).

Since $A,M,B$ are collinear,
$$\begin{align*}\angle AMO+\angle BMO&=180^\circ\\2\angle AMO&=180^\circ\\\angle AMO&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Thus $AB\perp OP$. Together with $AM=BM$, this proves that $OP$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$.
